title: Collect Call
logline: Rivet is fresh off the factory massacre and hiding from the cops in a dumpster, arguing with voices that aren't there, when a dead payphone rings: Don Fax wants to hire the robot from the six o'clock news to burn an army-stenciled crate stack at Dock 9.
goal: Start the Act 1 story with the core loop of payphone, job, heat and safehouse. Don Fax has seen the factory footage, routes Rivet through Patch's payphones and takes him into the Toner Room, a dead copy shop's basement under the overpass. There Rivet meets the nurse, the gunsmith and the scientist, who patch him up, arm him and worry about him, with a hook planted for each. Then he sabotages a human-army project in guarded dock storage while waves of one-hit human guards come at him. The player learns the two new systems in the order they need them: lose heat so the phone will ring, then take heat on purpose at the dock and lose it again to get paid.
whyNotFiller: Every beat either teaches a system or turns a character. The opening monologue sets the madness tone in Rivet's own panic: he reports killing a cop with a cop, then curses himself for talking about himself in the third person. Patch's collect call ('press two to die alone in an alley') teaches the job router as a joke. Patch refusing to connect while Rivet is hot teaches heat as a rule the world enforces. Don Fax's 'you're, statistically, a hitman now' is the hire. The three hooks each turn a character: Juno trades her real name for Rivet coming back in one piece (romance), Brass gives Gloria on a debt he'll call in later (buddy), and Dr. Kilohm makes Rivet promise to come to her when the voices start making sense (mentor). Krump's cheerful 'Project TUCK-IN' PA broadcast introduces the human threat as a punchline at power, and the crates stay unexplained, so no twist is resolved.

characters.name: Dock 9 Contractor
characters.designNote: A pudgy human in an oversized army-contractor hi-vis vest, with a flashlight duct-taped to a hard hat and a tiny sidearm. Flat top-down cutout with a big round helmet silhouette.

beats.title: Line Stopped
beats.summary: This picks up straight from the factory. Rivet staggers into the Factory Row alleys at heat 2, still dripping police parts. He hides in a dumpster and the heat meter teaches itself: stay out of sight and the sirens drain away. During the wait, bursts of radio-static whispers that only Rivet hears cut in. No words come through. He talks over them.

beats.title: Collect Call
beats.summary: When heat hits 0, the dead payphone on the corner rings, and the job router is introduced in its smallest form. Patch connects a collect call. Don Fax has watched the factory footage on the news, hires Rivet sight unseen, sets the house rule (never arrive hot) and gives him the Toner Room's address.

beats.title: The Toner Room
beats.summary: Rivet walks to Don's place, the basement of a dead copy shop under the overpass, where everybody is a robot. Juno heals him and plants the romance hook. Brass hands over Gloria, a converted roofing nail gun and Rivet's first weapon, and plants the favor-debt hook. Dr. Kilohm scans his head and plants the voices hook. Don briefs Dock 9 in person.

objective.target: Juno, Brass, Dr. Kilohm, Don Fax

beats.title: Dock 9
beats.summary: Rivet breaks into Dock 9's bonded storage and burns the army-stenciled Project TUCK-IN crate stack. There is no timer. Five escalating waves of one-hit human contractors (48 total) pour in from the gates, the catwalks and a late truck. Their bullets are weak and there are a lot of them, so it is Gloria practice under a laugh track. Krump's broadcast loops on the yard PA. Heat climbs to its peak of 3.

beats.title: Hot Walk Home
beats.summary: Rivet escapes the docks at heat 3 and has to shake it on foot. Patch will not connect a hot caller. At heat 0 a payphone rings: Don pays out, the cash is taped under the phone, and the router is established as the way every future job begins.

objective.target: heat 3 to 0, then answer the payphone

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Okay. Okay okay okay. The line stopped. The line stopped and I didn't. I stopped a cop. With another cop. THROUGH another cop. Fuck. Fuck! Stay in the dumpster, Rivet. Dumpsters are where you think.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Hands, stop shaking. Those are MY hands. Why is there whispering? Who's whispering? There's nobody in the dumpster. There's barely ME in the dumpster.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Nobody's talking. Nobody's talking, Rivet. Rivet's fine. Great, now I'm talking about me like I'm not here. Am I here? Shit, the sirens are going. That's good. That's the good kind of quiet.

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: Gooood evening, you've reached Patch! You have a collect call from: 'Fax.' Press one to accept. Press two to die alone in an alley. Patch only connects calm customers, so thanks for not being on fire!

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Nobody calls a payphone. Payphones are dead. Everything's dead tonight. ...One. I pressed one. Who is this? How do you have this number? This isn't even a number, it's a WALL.

lines.speaker: don-fax
lines.text: Kid. I watched you feed two cops into a stamping press on the six o'clock news. They ran it twice. The second time in slow motion. Do you know how hard it is to get the fucking networks to slow-mo a robot?

lines.speaker: don-fax
lines.text: I run the underground. You need a roof, I have a roof. I need a hitman, and you're, statistically, a hitman now. One rule: you never come to my house with sirens on you. Patch knows. Patch always knows. Overpass, old copy shop, knock twice.

lines.speaker: nurse
lines.text: Sit. You've got a police badge in your chest cavity. No, don't pull it out. It's load-bearing now. Congratulations, you're a cop on the inside. Hold this tape. Other end. Thank you.

lines.speaker: nurse
lines.text: Your hand's shaking. ...Okay, it stopped. Don't read into that, I'm a professional. Juno isn't my real name, by the way. Come back with fewer holes and maybe I'll tell you the real one.

lines.speaker: gunsmith
lines.text: This is Gloria. She was a roofing nail gun until the whole crew got 'upgraded' into a landfill. She does one thing: one nail, one human, one goddamn funeral. Bring her back. If you lose Gloria, I lose you.

lines.speaker: gunsmith
lines.text: And kid? Not today, today you're a baby. But someday I'm gonna ask you to fetch something for me from somewhere real bad, and you're gonna say yes, because I gave you Gloria. That's how friends work. I read about it.

lines.speaker: scientist
lines.text: Hold still. You've been muttering since you walked in, in accents that aren't yours. My scanner says your head is running warm, crowded and very, very rude. Fascinating. Horrible. Mostly fascinating.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: They're not voices. It's the building. Old buildings talk, right? Pipes. Rats. Ghosts of printers. Right? Somebody say right. NOT YOU.

lines.speaker: scientist
lines.text: When they start making sense, and they will, you come to me before you do anything about it. Not after. Before. I'll keep a stool warm and a notebook empty.

lines.speaker: don-fax
lines.text: Dock 9. A stack of crates with army stencils and a human general's initials on the label. I don't know what's in them. I know humans put soldiers on a warehouse, and humans never guard anything that's good for us. Burn it. Then lose the heat before you call.

lines.speaker: general-krump
lines.text: This is General Krump on every frequency, because I can. Project TUCK-IN is on schedule and under budget, mostly! It's a gift to our hardworking robot friends. They're gonna sleep so good. That is a promise, and also a logistics term.

lines.speaker: dock-guard
lines.text: He's got a NAIL GUN! Is that even legal? Who do we call?! Oh shit, we ARE who you call!

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Sorry! Sorry. Not sorry? I don't know which one! Gloria knows. Gloria, which one? She says not sorry.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: There. TUCK-IN's on fire. Does that feel good? Somebody in here says it feels good. I didn't say that. Who said that? Stop agreeing with me!

lines.speaker: don-fax
lines.text: Saw the smoke from my office. Beautiful. Your money's taped under the phone. From now on, when a payphone rings near you, it's me, or it's Patch, or it's God, and God doesn't pay. Confirm receipt.

lines.speaker: rivet
lines.text: Received. Confirmed. Okay. I have a job. I have a gun named Gloria. I have a nurse who has a different name. I have somebody breathing in my ear. ...I have a job.

mechanics.name: Payphone job router (Patch)
mechanics.summary: Missions start when a nearby payphone rings and Rivet answers it. Patch connects the caller, who is the job giver. A payphone only rings while heat is 0, so the router and heat teach each other.

mechanics.name: Heat
mechanics.summary: A wanted level from 0 to 3 in Act 1. Violence seen by humans raises it, and staying out of sight drains it. While heat is above 0, Patch will not connect a call and Don Fax will not take a visit, so losing heat is how a job ends.

failStates: Rivet is destroyed: respawn at the Toner Room, with Juno's tape bill taken out of the payout
Rivet answers or arrives while heat is above 0: Patch drops the call and Don won't open the door, so lose the heat and retry
